# git edit

Add `git edit <sha>`: amend an arbitrary earlier commit with the changes currently in the working tree, driven end-to-end:

```bash
$ git edit sha1
# git rebase -i sha1^
# git stash pop
# git add .
# git amend
# git rebase --continue
```

i.e. stash the changes, start an interactive rebase at the commit's parent with that commit marked `edit`, pop the stash, amend, and finish the rebase — the manual routine for "this fix belongs in that commit".
